Younger brother of Amago Tsunehisa. A capable aide to his brother, he helps lay the foundation for the Amago clan's rise.

Younger brother of Amago Tsunehisa. A capable aide to his brother, he helps lay the foundation for the Amago clan's rise.
When Haruhisa moves to punish the Mouri for defecting from the Amago to the Ouchi, Hisayuki urges him not to, only to be called a coward for it. (Ep. 6)

Younger brother of Amago Tsunehisa. A capable aide to his brother, he helps lay the foundation for the Amago clan's rise.
When Haruhisa moves to punish the Mouri for defecting from the Amago to the Ouchi, Hisayuki urges him not to, only to be called a coward for it. Yet at the Battle of Yoshida-Koriyama Castle, as his side collapses, he fights fiercely, crying, "Watch how a coward meets his end!" and dies in battle.
(Ep. 6)
note: Quoted cry worded after Hisayuki's own line in the script (U01601).

en: Son of Amago Kunihisa. With his father, he leads the Shinguto, a formidable band of warriors.

Son of Amago Kunihisa. With his father, he leads the Shinguto, a formidable band of warriors.
At the Battle of Yoshida-Koriyama Castle, he marches on the castle with Amago Haruhisa. (Ep. 6)

Son of Amago Kunihisa. With his father, he leads the Shinguto, a formidable band of warriors.
At the Battle of Yoshida-Koriyama Castle, he marches on the castle with Amago Haruhisa. (Ep. 6)
In the Interception in Bingo, he appears with his father, Kunihisa, at the head of the Amago Army's main force.
(Ep. 8)

Son of Amago Kunihisa. With his father, he leads the Shinguto, a formidable band of warriors.
At the Battle of Yoshida-Koriyama Castle, he marches on the castle with Amago Haruhisa. (Ep. 6)
In the Interception in Bingo, he appears with his father, Kunihisa, at the head of the Amago Army's main force.
(Ep. 8)
In the Westward Push through Aki, he appears and strikes at the rear of the Mouri Army as it moves against the Ouchi Army, and tries to take Yoshida-Koriyama Castle. (Ep. 11)

Son of Amago Kunihisa. With his father, he leads the Shinguto, a formidable band of warriors.
At the Battle of Yoshida-Koriyama Castle, he marches on the castle with Amago Haruhisa. (Ep. 6)
In the Interception in Bingo, he appears with his father, Kunihisa, at the head of the Amago Army's main force.
(Ep. 8)
But Haruhisa, deceived by the Mouri Army's scheme, suspects him of treason, and he is killed together with his father, Kunihisa.
(Ep. 11)
Second son of Amago Haruhisa and younger brother of Yoshihisa.

Second son of Amago Haruhisa and younger brother of Yoshihisa.
In the Siege of Shiraga Castle, he rushes from Gassan-Toda Castle with Amago reinforcements and confronts the Mouri Army. (Ep. 16)

Second son of Amago Haruhisa and younger brother of Yoshihisa.
In the Siege of Shiraga Castle, he rushes from Gassan-Toda Castle with Amago reinforcements and confronts the Mouri Army. (Ep. 16)
In the Siege of Gassan-Toda Castle, he is captured with Yoshihisa when the castle falls, and is afterward held captive in Aki. (Ep. 18)
Eldest son of Amago Haruhisa. He inherits the headship after his father's sudden death.

Eldest son of Amago Haruhisa. He inherits the headship after his father's sudden death.
In the Siege of Gassan-Toda Castle, he is captured when the castle falls and is held captive in Aki. With this, the Amago clan falls. (Ep. 18)
A local lord of Aki based at Komeyama Castle. Said to descend from Amano Tokage, a distinguished Minamoto vassal of the Kamakura period.

A local lord of Aki based at Komeyama Castle. Said to descend from Amano Tokage, a distinguished Minamoto vassal of the Kamakura period.
In the Siege of Kagamiyama Castle, he takes the Ouchi side and confronts the Mouri and Kikkawa armies, which have advanced as far as the foot of Kagamiyama Castle as the Amago vanguard. (Ep. 2)
Lord of Saizaki Castle in Aki. He owes allegiance to the Ouchi clan.

Lord of Saizaki Castle in Aki. He once owed allegiance to the Ouchi clan.
In the Siege of Kagamiyama Castle, he confronts the Mouri and Kikkawa armies, which have advanced to the foot of Kagamiyama Castle as the Amago vanguard. Persuaded by Motonari, he surrenders and becomes a Mouri retainer. (Ep. 2)

A novice monk at Ankoku-ji. He guides Mouri Takamoto, lost while hunting, to the temple. (Ep. 10)

The surviving son of Takeda Nobushige, lord of Kanayama Castle, whose house the Mouri destroyed. Left in the care of Ankoku-ji when the castle fell, he became a novice monk.
He guides Mouri Takamoto, lost while hunting, to the temple, and the two become close friends. (Ep. 10)

The surviving son of Takeda Nobushige, lord of Kanayama Castle, whose house the Mouri destroyed. Left in the care of Ankoku-ji when the castle fell, he became a novice monk.

When Takamoto is poisoned by Amago ninja, it falls to him to be with Takamoto at the end. (Ep. 16)

A Tokugawa retainer. Counted with Honda Tadakatsu and others among the "Four Heavenly Kings of the Tokugawa," he always leads the vanguard in battle.
A hereditary Tokugawa retainer, he shows his talent chiefly in diplomacy.

en:
A Sengoku daimyo ruling Suruga, Totomi and Mikawa. He marches on Kyoto to bring the realm under his command, but is struck down by Oda Nobunaga at Okehazama and dies in battle.
(Ep. 15)
An Amago retainer and one of the Ten Braves of Amago. Even after the Mouri destroy the Amago, he works tirelessly with Yamanaka Shikanosuke and others to restore the clan.

An Amago retainer and one of the Ten Braves of Amago. Even after the Mouri destroy the Amago, he works tirelessly with Yamanaka Shikanosuke and others to restore the clan.
At the Battle of Mount Fube, he clashes with the Mouri Army in a bid to retake Gassan-Toda Castle. (Ep. 20)

An Amago retainer and one of the Ten Braves of Amago. Even after the Mouri destroy the Amago, he works tirelessly with Yamanaka Shikanosuke and others to restore the clan.
At the Battle of Mount Fube, he clashes with the Mouri Army in a bid to retake Gassan-Toda Castle. (Ep. 20)
In the Bizen Campaign, he appears with the Amago remnants and faces Mouri Terumoto, but for all his hard fighting, he dies in battle.
(Ep. 21)

Younger half-brother of Ukita Naoie. As Naoie's strategist, he devotes himself to the rise of the Ukita clan.
In the Bizen Campaign, he leaves Okayama Castle, sets up camp and confronts the Mouri Army. (Ep. 21)

A Sengoku daimyo of Bizen. While serving the Urakami clan, he uses all manner of schemes to revive the declining Ukita clan, then overthrows his lord to become a daimyo.
At the Otomo clan's instigation, he joins the encirclement of the Mouri, invades Bitchu and defeats Mimura Motochika. (Ep. 19)

A Sengoku daimyo of Bizen. While serving the Urakami clan, he uses all manner of schemes to revive the declining Ukita clan, then overthrows his lord to become a daimyo.
At the Otomo clan's instigation, he joins the encirclement of the Mouri, invades Bitchu and defeats Mimura Motochika. (Ep. 19)
In the Bizen Campaign, he surrenders to the Mouri Army as it advances on Okayama Castle. (Ep. 21)

A Sengoku daimyo of Bizen. While serving the Urakami clan, he uses all manner of schemes to revive the declining Ukita clan, then overthrows his lord to become a daimyo.
At the Otomo clan's instigation, he joins the encirclement of the Mouri, invades Bitchu and defeats Mimura Motochika. (Ep. 19)
In the Bizen Campaign, he surrenders to the Mouri Army as it advances on Okayama Castle. (Ep. 21)
But when Hashiba Hideyoshi's forces close in on Bizen, he defects again, this time to the Oda clan. (Ep. 23)
An Amago retainer. He serves among the house elders and holds a domain worth as much as 100,000 koku.

An Amago retainer. He serves among the house elders and holds a domain worth as much as 100,000 koku.
In the Interception in Bingo, he leads the Amago Army's advance force with Kamei Hidetsuna and attacks Miyoshi Takasuke's Hiebiyama Castle.
(Ep. 7)
An Otomo retainer. With Yoshihiro Akimasa and others, he is one of the Three Elders of Bungo who assist Otomo Sorin.

An Otomo retainer. With Yoshihiro Akimasa and others, he is one of the Three Elders of Bungo who assist Otomo Sorin.
In the Struggle for Moji Castle, he leads a fleet with the pirates of Bungo and confronts the Mouri Army as it closes in on Moji Castle.
(Ep. 14)

An Otomo retainer. With Yoshihiro Akimasa and others, he is one of the Three Elders of Bungo who assist Otomo Sorin.
In the Struggle for Moji Castle, he leads a fleet with the pirates of Bungo and confronts the Mouri Army as it closes in on Moji Castle.
(Ep. 14)
In the Chikuzen Campaign, he marches out to take Homanzan Castle, where the rebel Takahashi Akitane is holed up. (Ep. 19)
A local lord of Iyo. Based at Ozu Castle, he is on close terms with the Otomo clan.

A local lord of Iyo. Based at Ozu Castle, he is on close terms with the Otomo clan.
At the Battle of Ozu Castle, he is on the offensive against the Kono Army of Iyo, but when the Mouri come to the Kono's aid, he asks the Otomo for reinforcements. Even so, he is defeated by the Mouri Army's onslaught. (Ep. 18)
An Amago retainer. A loyal vassal who struggles desperately to hold up the Amago clan as it crumbles before the Mouri onslaught.

An Amago retainer. A loyal vassal who struggles desperately to hold up the Amago clan as it crumbles before the Mouri onslaught.
But in the Siege of Gassan-Toda Castle, a Mouri scheme leads his lord, Amago Yoshihisa, to suspect him of secretly siding with the enemy, and he is put to death. (Ep. 17)

An Amago retainer. A loyal vassal who struggles desperately to hold up the Amago clan as it crumbles before the Mouri onslaught.
In the Siege of Gassan-Toda Castle, he fights back from inside the castle against the Mouri Army's onslaught. (Ep. 17)
A local lord of Bingo, based at Hatagaeshi Castle.

A local lord of Bingo, based at Hatagaeshi Castle.
In the Pacification of Aki and Bingo, he is at first on the Ouchi side, but when Amago Haruhisa's forces appear in Bingo, he defects to the Amago. (Ep. 10)
An Ouchi retainer. A fierce general who excels in field battles.

An Ouchi retainer. A fierce general who excels in field battles.
At the Battle of Yoshida-Koriyama Castle, he rushes in with Sue Harukata as reinforcements for the Mouri. (Ep. 6)

An Ouchi retainer. A fierce general who excels in field battles.
At the Battle of Yoshida-Koriyama Castle, he rushes in with Sue Harukata as reinforcements for the Mouri. (Ep. 6)
When Sue Harukata rebels, he marches out with him and strikes down their lord, Ouchi Yoshitaka. (Ep. 10)

An Ouchi retainer. A fierce general who excels in field battles.
At the Battle of Yoshida-Koriyama Castle, he rushes in with Sue Harukata to support the Mouri. (Ep. 6)
When Sue Harukata rebels, he marches out with him and strikes down their lord, Ouchi Yoshitaka. (Ep. 10)
But before the Battle of Itsukushima, a Mouri scheme leads Harukata to suspect him of secretly siding with the enemy, and he is put to death. (Ep. 12)

An Ouchi retainer. A fierce general who excels in field battles.
At the Battle of Yoshida-Koriyama Castle, he rushes in with Sue Harukata to support the Mouri. (Ep. 6)
When Sue Harukata rebels, he marches out with him and strikes down their lord, Ouchi Yoshitaka. (Ep. 10)
At the Battle of Itsukushima, he deploys between the Mouri Army's main force and Miyao Castle and confronts the Mouri Army. (Ep. 12)
Younger brother of Ouchi Yoshioki, which makes him Yoshitaka's uncle. After falling out with his kin, he leaves the Ouchi clan and takes refuge with the Otomo clan.

Younger brother of Ouchi Yoshioki, which makes him Yoshitaka's uncle. After falling out with his kin, he leaves the Ouchi clan and takes refuge with the Otomo clan.
In the Chikuzen Campaign, he comes to the aid of the Otomo and threatens the rear of the Mouri Army, which has invaded Chikuzen. (Ep. 19)

A daimyo whose power covers northern Kyushu and western Chugoku. Escorting the former Shogun Ashikaga Yoshitane, he marches on Kyoto, restores Yoshitane as Shogun, and directs the shogunate's government as acting shogunal deputy.

A daimyo whose power covers northern Kyushu and western Chugoku. Escorting the former Shogun Ashikaga Yoshitane, he marches on Kyoto, restores Yoshitane as Shogun, and directs the shogunate's government as acting shogunal deputy. But alarmed by the Amago clan's growing power, he resigns the post and returns to Yamaguchi. (Ep. 2)
note: [edit: "Shogun" capitalised as the holder's title, per the shared profile style]

en:
A daimyo whose power covers northern Kyushu and western Chugoku. Escorting the former Shogun Ashikaga Yoshitane, he marches on Kyoto, restores Yoshitane as Shogun, and directs the shogunate's government as acting shogunal deputy. But alarmed by the Amago clan's growing power, he resigns the post and returns to Yamaguchi. (Ep. 2)
After the fall of Kagamiyama and a long standoff with the Amago, he sends troops against Kanayama Castle, held by Takeda Mitsukazu.
(Ep. 4)
